studies.Study: Wu JW et al. (2012) [PMID: 22568968] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Dietary intake of meat, fruits, vegetables, and selective micronutrients and risk of bladder cancer in the New England region of the United States.
studies.Title: Dietary intake of meat, fruits, vegetables, and selective micronutrients and risk of bladder cancer in the New England region of the United States.
studies.Authors: Wu JW, Cross AJ, Baris D, Ward MH, Karagas MR, Johnson A, Schwenn M, Cherala S, Colt JS, Cantor KP, Rothman N, Silverman DT, Sinha R
studies.Population: residents of Maine, New Hampshire, and Vermont
studies.Smoking Status: Never, occasional, former, and current smokers included and adjusted for
studies.comparison_type: highest vs lowest quartile of dietary vitamin B12 intake

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 1171 cases were ascertained through hospital pathology records and cancer registries from 2001 to 2004. Overall, 1418 controls were identified from the Department of Motor Vehicles (<65 years) and Center for Medicaid and Medicare Services (65-79 years) and were frequency-matched to cases by state, sex, and age (within 5 years).
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 1171 + 1418 = 2589

cases.excerpt: A total of 1171 cases were ascertained through hospital pathology records and cancer registries from 2001 to 2004.

effect_size.excerpt: We did, however, observe an inverse association with vitamin B12 intake (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61-0.99; P=0.019).

confidence_interval.excerpt: We did, however, observe an inverse association with vitamin B12 intake (OR: 0.77; 95% CI: 0.61-0.99; P=0.019).

design.excerpt: We conducted a population-based case-control study of bladder cancer

continent.excerpt: New England region of the United States

ethnicity.excerpt: The majority of the study subjects were White (94.5% and 94.7% for cases and controls, respectively).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Diet was assessed with a self-administered Diet History Questionnaire.

gender.excerpt: frequency-matched to cases by state, sex, and age
